title: Artemis II lunar flash evidence

findings.proposition: The public annotation contains five accepted events, eight witness marks, and three observers.
findings.claim_ceiling: Credible event ledger, not calibrated sensitivity or independent detections.

findings.proposition: The later 30 fps window covered the annotation's 01:04 background-photo epoch.
findings.claim_ceiling: Metadata-time non-overlap only. The photo epoch is not ledger creation or an upper bound for all five accepted events; their event-level video coverage remains unestablished.

findings.proposition: The absence of a screened pulse in the overlap clip excludes the shared crew report.
findings.claim_ceiling: Contextual temporal overlap, not event exclusion.

findings.proposition: Five accepted events support a conservative whole-Moon one-hour detected-count floor.
findings.claim_ceiling: Detected-count floor under explicit assumptions, not calibrated flux.

findings.proposition: The five events establish a calibrated brightness-threshold lunar impact flux.
findings.claim_ceiling: Blocked until a recomputable measurement function is public.

findings.proposition: The two marks around the 00:51 report are independent confirmations suitable for capture-recapture inference.
findings.claim_ceiling: Separate witness marks are preserved, but independence is not assumed without a declared dependence model.

claim_ceiling: This case may establish the annotated witness pattern, selected transcript anchors, metadata-time non-overlap with the background-photo epoch, the poor clip-native recovery of one contextual screen, and a conservative detected-count floor. It does not certify ledger creation, bound all five event times, certify coverage or noncoverage of every accepted event, map reports one-to-one to numbered events, establish independent witnesses, exclude a reported flash, estimate calibrated physical flux, prove every candidate's cause, or accept an operational recommendation on NASA's behalf.
next_steps: Publish event-level time intervals or uncertainty bounds before mapping transcript reports to numbered events.
Publish verified live time, monitored area, radiometric response, limiting sensitivity, and task-shaped injection recovery before estimating flux.
Declare a witness-dependence model before treating prompted or socially cued marks as independent detections.
Bind every future camera null to event coverage, target-in-field evidence, and a passed capability gate.
